content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure.

input.summary: Full source ledger built and traced. Every limitation of all 22 claims (independent claims 1, 13, 18 and dependent claims 2-12, 14-17, 19-22), every entry in the numeral ledger (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94), every numbered part in the detailed description, and every structure, relationship, material, result, and operating step in the summary, abstract, Brief Description of the Drawings, and the seven figure briefs was traced to an exact affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md (the USER text in input/conversation.md is an identical but truncated copy and adds nothing). No untraced technical assertion was found: the rail/flat lower face/longitudinal slot/printed distance marks, the perpendicular fixed fence with its downwardly projecting portion, the two-screw reversible mounting that moves that portion from one longitudinal side to the opposite side while the marked upper face keeps facing the user, the removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces that changes setback by its thickness without changing separation, the two separate guide carriages with anti-rotation keys in the slot, the cylindrical hardened-metal replaceable drill bushings whose bores pass completely through the carriage, register with the slot, and are parallel to one another and perpendicular to the flat lower face, the threaded clamp knobs whose shanks reach clamping shoes below the rail, the two pointers aligned with their bore axes whose reading difference is the center-to-center spacing, the transverse center index at the midpoint, the shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with that index and with the pencil centerline, the rigid-polymer-or-metal material list, and the no-motor/no-battery/no-sensor/no-network recitations all correspond to affirmative disclosure sentences. Section-line designations 3-3 and 5-5 carry the same repeated designation in the FIG. 2 source-view brief, in the resulting FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 briefs, and in the Brief Description of the Drawings; every numeral means one thing throughout and each appears in at least one figure brief; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative remains; the schematic generic outlines (plain blocks, plain round bodies, plain rectangular fence body) stay confined to the figure briefs and are not verbalized as embodiments or "by way of example" in the application text, and the shallow V-notch and parallel-faced spacer plate geometry that the briefs do verbalize is taken verbatim from the disclosure. Two internal-consistency defects remain, both in the drawing specifications and neither affecting source fidelity: the transverse section-plane briefs for FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 place the clamp-knob shank and the drill-bushing bore in a single un-offset cutting plane although both must pass through the same longitudinal slot at different points along the rail, and the FIG. 7 brief gives two mutually exclusive page-placement instructions. Fixes for both are stated below.

findings.title: Section-plane briefs for FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 place the clamp-knob shank and the drill-bushing bore in one un-offset transverse cutting plane
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (cutting-plane line paragraphs), figures/FIG-3.md, figures/FIG-5.md; draft/08-detailed-description.md ("a cross-sectional view taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 2 through the second guide carriage 70")
findings.detail: FIG-2.md specifies each cutting-plane line as a single straight line "aligned transverse to the length of the rail 10" crossing a carriage. FIG-3.md and FIG-5.md then require that same single transverse plane to show, at once, the threaded shank passing "through the carriage 70 and the slot 16, and into a clamping shoe 80" and the drill bushing whose "vertical bore passing completely through the carriage 70 and aligned with the slot 16." Both the shank and the bore are recited (claims 1, 13, 18; description) as registering with the same longitudinal slot, so they necessarily lie at different stations along the rail's length and cannot both be intersected by one straight transverse cutting plane. As briefed, a renderer must either place the bore and the shank side by side across the rail's width, which contradicts "registers with the longitudinal slot" for one of them, or draw one of them outside the cut. This is a drawing-consistency defect only; the underlying structures are fully supported by the disclosure ("A threaded shank of the knob passes through the carriage and the longitudinal slot into a clamping shoe below the rail"; "The bore passes completely through the carriage and aligns with an opening through the slot").
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md: "A broken cutting-plane line crosses the second guide carriage 70, aligned transverse to the length of the rail 10." FIG-3.md: "A threaded shank extends from the knob, through the carriage 70 and the slot 16, and into a clamping shoe 80 located below the rail 10." and "A cylindrical drill bushing 74 is carried by the carriage 70, its vertical bore passing completely through the carriage 70 and aligned with the slot 16." FIG-5.md repeats both statements for the shank of clamp knob 58, clamping shoe 60, and drill bushing 54.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, make each section line an offset (stepped) cutting-plane line. Replace the first cutting-plane sentence with: "A broken cutting-plane line crosses the second guide carriage 70 transverse to the length of the rail 10 along the axis of the bore of that carriage, jogs longitudinally within the outline of the second guide carriage 70, and continues transversely along the axis of the threaded shank of the clamp knob of that carriage." Replace the corresponding sentence for the second line with the same wording referring to the first guide carriage 50. Keep the existing endpoint, arrow-direction, and designation sentences unchanged, so the lines remain line 3-3 and line 5-5 in the FIG. 2 brief, in figures/FIG-3.md and figures/FIG-5.md, and in draft/07-drawings.md. No change to the application text is required.

findings.title: FIG. 7 brief gives two mutually exclusive page-placement instructions for the workpiece
findings.detail: The brief instructs that the workpiece panel both "fills the drawing area" and is "well clear of the drawing area borders." A depicted element that fills the drawing area necessarily reaches its borders, so the two instructions cannot both be followed. Every other figure brief uses only the margin-preserving form (FIG-1.md "well inside the drawing area"; FIG-2.md "well clear of the drawing area borders"; FIG-4.md "The whole view lies well inside the drawing area"). This is a non-substantive placement instruction only and carries no invention content, but it is an internal contradiction in the drawing specification.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-7.md: "The workpiece 90 is a flat panel seen from above and fills the drawing area, well clear of the drawing area borders."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-7.md, replace that sentence with: "The workpiece 90 is a flat panel seen from above and occupies most of the drawing area, well clear of the drawing area borders." No change to the application text is required.
